title: Etale extension by zero commutes with base change for module sheaves
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $j:V\to X$ be etale, and form the fibre-product square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $V'=Y\times_XV$, $j':V'\to Y$, and $f':V'\to V$. For a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda_V$-modules on $V_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the base-change morphism $\beta_M:j'_!((f')^{-1}M)\to f^{-1}(j_!M)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], where inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] on sheaves of modules [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and $j_!$, $j'_!$ are etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y$-modules. Hence $\beta^{-1}$ is an isomorphism $f^{-1}(j_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!((f')^{-1}M)$, natural in $M$. This is Stacks Project Lemma 59.70.5, Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), in the module-sheaf form.

proof.text: Unfold `etaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap`. The exchange transformation is an isomorphism by the existing étale base-change theorem `Etale.isIso_baseChangeMap_flip_of_isPullback` applied to the pullback square `IsPullback.of_hasPullback f j` (flipped). The typeclass instance `conjugateEquiv_symm_iso` then makes its conjugate defining the lower-shriek base-change map an isomorphism. The existing exchange theorem combines the restriction identification and its isomorphism recorded by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction], with coefficients in ModuleCat Λ; [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] supplies preservation of isomorphisms under inverse conjugation.

split_report.summary: The canonical base-change morphism of the statement was defined in no node. It is now defined in the new node def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map as the conjugate, for the composite adjunctions f^{-1}j_! -| j^{-1}f_* and j'_!f'^{-1} -| f'_*j'^{-1}, of the underived exchange Ex^0: j^{-1}f_* -> f'_*j'^{-1}. With that definition it runs j'_!f'^{-1}M -> f^{-1}j_!M. This is the direction a conjugate of the exchange has without first inverting it, and the direction of the slopmaster2 open-immersion analogue. The statement is corrected to this direction, cites the new definition, and states the inverse iso f^{-1}j_!M -> j'_!f'^{-1}M explicitly, which is what the only citer (lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible) uses. The proof follows Stacks 03S6 exactly: compare the right adjoints. The abelian isomorphism of the right adjoints is the closed node lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction (unit sk-thm-reduction, a tool since it is closed). Its Lambda-linearity is the new node lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear. The conclusion uses the Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate. The adjunction j_! -| j^{-1} is taken from lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives (unit sk-thm-iff, on route); f^{-1} -| f_* on modules is taken from prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (sk-def-exchange, on route). Stalk descriptions (03S5) and the free-module case lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-free-etale-module are not needed.
